correctness.rationale: The source gives the minimal secant-degree formula and proves rational normal scrolls attain it. Specializing the one-dimensional scroll S(d) gives \(D_{d,k}=\binom{d-k}{k+1}\) in the proper range. Kummer then gives the exact prime-adic carry count. For parity, Lucas modulo two reduces oddness to binary support containment. When \(d+2\) is a power of two, \(d+1\) is an all-ones binary word and every admissible subtraction produces the complementary low bits, forcing evenness. Otherwise, \(a=2^{\nu_2(d+2)}\) is the first admissible lower index whose bit survives in \(d+1-a\), while every smaller positive \(a\) fails Lucas. The proof covers all quantifiers and boundary cases.

value.rationale: Higher secant varieties are central projective invariants of rational normal curves, and their degrees count complementary linear sections. The result converts the entire classical degree tower into an exact carry statistic at every prime and gives a complete binary phase transition: precisely the dimensions \(d=2^m-2\) have no odd proper secant degree, while every other dimension has an explicit first odd stage. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
